name: negative-interactive-shell
description: Interactive login shell that happens to satisfy the sequence shape, NOT a reverse shell. A login shell (bash, argv[0]='-bash', i.e. a TTY/interactive login such as an SSH or console session) is exec'd, connects to a callback port (4444), and redirects stdio — so the bounded sequence WOULD complete cleanly. However, the interactive/login-shell exception (process.argv contains '-bash') matches the exec event and suppresses the alert. This fixture isolates the exception mechanism: the sequence completes but the safe exception decides the outcome. A real reverse shell runs the interpreter non-login (argv like ['bash','-i']), which does NOT carry the '-bash' login marker. Expect no match.
